1.1: 1.1 RABANUS, exposition on the book of Esther, vol. 3. The book of Esther, which the Hebrews number among the hagiographa, contains the sacraments of Christ and the Church, etc., down to who reigned after Darius his uncle surnamed Nochus forty years.
1.2: 1.2 Susa, a city, etc. Susa is a metropolis in Persia, which historians say was founded by the brother of Memnon, and took its name from the river Susis. There is the royal house of Cyrus of white and variegated stone, with golden columns, with coffered ceilings and gems distinguished: containing an image of heaven marked with shining stars, and many incredible things. There Ahasuerus held a very great banquet with riches and abundant delights. For the power of the sacred utterance sometimes so narrates things past as to express things to come: so approves the maker as to contradict him in ministry: so condemns deeds as to persuade that they are to be done mystically.
1.3: 1.3 In the third year therefore. In the time, namely, of this age he revealed the sacrament of his incarnation, and abundantly ministered the spiritual feasts of preaching, and of his body and blood. The first time before the law, the second under the law, the third under grace. A great banquet for all the princes. The kingdom of heaven is like a man a king who made a marriage for his son, Matthew 22. And elsewhere: A certain man made a great supper: and invited many, Luke 14. The history of this banquet shows the pomp of riches and the luxury of the king: but allegorically it signifies the spiritual delights of Christ which he dispenses to each. For Christ is that most rich king, who, entreated by the prayers of his wife, that is the Church, delivers the Jews, that is his confessors, from the hand of enemies, and justly condemns those same. Nor is it necessary, if the goods of some signify Christ, that their evils also suit Christ himself. For Moses in many things signified Christ; but not in this, that he doubted at the waters of contradiction. Nor Aaron in the making of the calf. Nor Solomon in the filth of lust. So Ahasuerus in this judgment, as in the liberal banquet, signifies Christ, as Isaiah in Cyrus king of the Persians signifies Christ, of whom afterwards he adds: I girded you, and you have not known me, Isaiah 45, etc. For if wicked kings in evil deeds signify the devil, why do not just kings in good deeds show Christ? Nebuchadnezzar commanded the peoples, prostrate on hearing the voice of symphonies and musicians, to adore the statue. And the devil by worldly sweetness bends the human race from rectitude of mind to follow covetousness which is the service of idols.
1.5: 1.5 The days of the banquet. The great or the first of the faithful were the first refreshed, according to that: I am not sent but to the sheep that are lost of the house of Israel, Matthew 15. In the sacrament of circumcision of the Lord's resurrection, and of the New Testament and true circumcision: and there are eight beatitudes, to which this banquet leads, which is held only by days; but the wicked feasted in nights.
1.6: 1.6 And there hung. Fine linen signifies the mortification of the flesh. Purple, the blood of martyrdom. Marble columns, the firmness of teachers. Well therefore it is said that hangings of diverse colors, of linen and purple cords, were hung through ivory rings on marble columns; because the beauty of the Church ought to shine in teachers in the meditation of wisdom and in the ascent of the virtues through mortification of the flesh and chastity with the dignity of martyrdom; and through their word and example come to the knowledge of others: that, instructed and strengthened by them, they may deserve to enter the hall of paradise. And were supported by marble columns. That is, by teachers of whom it is said: I have strengthened its columns, Psalm 74. And elsewhere: He made silver columns, a golden couch, Canticle 3. Upon the pavement. The emerald is so called from its great greenness. Parian, a kind of very white marble. For through the greenness of faith and the whiteness of chastity the foundation of humility is built. For blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven, Matthew 5. And: He that humbles himself shall be exalted, Luke 10. And elsewhere: Learn of me, because I am meek, Matthew 11, etc.
1.7: 1.7 Wine. According to that: The charity of God is poured forth in our hearts, Romans 5, etc. To one is given the word of knowledge, to another of wisdom, to another faith, to another the grace of healing. He would not compel the unwilling to drink, etc. No one is compelled to receive a spiritual gift: God wants children, not servants: he wants will, not necessity, according to that: He that can take it, let him take it, Matthew 19. Likewise: If you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments, ibid. And: If you wish to be perfect, go and sell all you have, ibid., etc.
1.8: 1.8 Each what he would, etc. According to the quickness and capacity and usefulness of each. For preaching must be so tempered that in all it becomes useful, harms none, and passes through the vices of all like a two-edged sword. So that by pride cutting away it takes away, but does not increase timidity. So that, laying the solicitude of work on the idle and sluggish, it does not increase importunate action in the restless and curious, and so with the rest.
1.9: 1.9 In the palace, where King Ahasuerus, etc. Jerusalem, where the temple and the Holy of Holies, or in the meditation of holy Scripture; in which the Deity gave knowledge of his power.
1.11: 1.11 To show, etc. Where the fullness of time came, God sent his Son, Galatians 4, etc. For then the Son of God incarnate manifested with more abundant grace the mysteries of the law with which he had before fed the faithful.
1.12: 1.12 Who refused. Despising not only the messengers but also the king's command; hence in the Gospel, the elder son, asked by the father to the banquet, would not go in: and those who were called to the supper, occupied with other things, would not come, were, according to the indignation of the householder, rejected and others set in their place.
1.16: 1.16 And Memucan answered in the hearing of the king and the princes: Not only the king has the queen wronged, etc. He, counted last in the order of the seven wise men, pronounces sentence, and signifies Paul the apostle who says: I am the least of the apostles, who am not worthy to be called an apostle, 1 Corinthians 15. And to the Jews contradicting and filled with zeal he says: Because you judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold we turn to the Gentiles, Acts 13.
2.7: 2.7 Who was. Esther is interpreted hidden, Edissa, having obtained mercy. This is the Church of the Gentiles, which, nourishing in the hiddenness of the heart the chastity of faith, found mercy and grace before the eyes of the Lord, the synagogue being repudiated, which in Hosea was called without mercy. Her the spiritual Mordecai nourishes, and adopts as a daughter, who is the teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth, and is of the stock of Jemini, that is of the stock of Benjamin.
2.8: 2.8 Esther. Nebuchadnezzar, spiritual and king of confusion, translated her from the natural law and the worship of one God into the confusion of idolatry, but divine piety recalled her to the way of truth through preachers.
2.9: 2.9 And seven maidens. That is, faithful souls regenerated and dedicated by the grace of the Holy Spirit who follow his footsteps, in faith, teaching, and work, of whom it is said: The young maidens have loved you exceedingly. Who would not. Because cleansed by baptism from the stain of sins and the filth of idolatry, she would no longer endure the reproach of her former iniquity.
2.13: 2.13 And entering. Whatever soul strives to hasten to the bridal chamber of Christ receives a fitting adornment from her teachers, and the more she prepares herself devoted to the recognition of faith and the exercise of work, the more she is instructed by teachers, that from the number of the competent she may come to the entire faith and confession of the holy Trinity and the reception of baptism and the anointing of chrism, that she may truly be joined to the heavenly Bridegroom.
2.14: 2.14 And from thence. He who has separated himself from the Church by the filth of vices is deservedly thrust back to the second house where the king's concubines dwell: because a fall from sound faith deserves a descent of honor, nor has he further power to return to the king, unless, visited by heavenly grace, he is restored to the state of his former dignity.
2.15: 2.15 And when had passed. That is, five ages of the world having passed, in which the offspring of the fathers had gone forth, the sixth age was at hand with the coming of the Redeemer, in which the multitude of the Gentiles was to be called through the Gospel.
2.16: 2.16 Tebeth. Among the Hebrews; Xudimos among the Greeks; January among the Latins. In which the Lord incarnate was circumcised on the eighth day, adored by the Magi, and honored with mystical gifts, in which also he is proclaimed to have been baptized by John.
2.19: 2.19 And when also the second time. It is not enough for Christ to join to himself the primitive Church, but through preachers from the Gentiles he acquired a copious multitude; hence: Other sheep I have that are not, etc., John 10.
2.21: 2.21 Two eunuchs of the king, etc. In the two eunuchs schismatics and heretics can be noted, who, bearing in the heart the poison of fraud and malice, plot against the truth to take it from believers, and to kill Christ, that is the faith of Christ, in the faithful themselves: but the holy teachers make their iniquity manifest, that the innocent may be saved and those punished by just retribution.
2.23: 2.23 Handed down in histories and annals before the king, etc. In the two Testaments, in which it is written what rewards are due to the just, what punishments to the unjust; hence: These shall go into everlasting punishment: but the just into life everlasting, Matthew 25. And in Ezekiel: The justice of the just shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him, Ezekiel 18.
3.1: 3.1 Haman son of. The powerful of the age, who abusing the benefits conferred by divine power disdain to have as partners in grace those whom they have as partners in nature: and the honor and reverence which they owed to God alone they strive to transfer to themselves. Those who will not consent they pursue with hatred and tortures: but by the just judgment of God the wicked are caught in their own snares. Hence it is said: The just is delivered out of distress, and the wicked shall be given for him, Proverbs 11. By Haman, whom Josephus mentions to be of the stock of Amalek, the Jewish people can be figured: who killed the prophets, and the Lord of the prophets and the apostles, losing the nobility of that race by unbelief and hardness of heart, who through Isaiah are called princes of Sodom and people of Gomorrah. Hence Ezekiel: Your father an Amorite, and your mother a Hittite.
3.7: 3.7 The lot was cast. Those who belong to the Lord's lot are slain, whom that goat signifies, which according to the Lord's lot was slain in the law.
3.10: 3.10 He took therefore. As Haman, sending letters, tries to fortify them with the king's seal: that the wish may be more easily accomplished, so the Jews take the books of the divine law, in which is the seal of the supreme King, that is the grace of the Holy Spirit, as witness to comprehend their heresy, rejecting the fellowship of the Gentiles and the Gospel of Christ, as contrary to the divine precepts.
4.2: 4.2 Even to the gate. So the master of the Church by the intercession of the queen, of whom it is said: The queen stood on your right hand, Psalm 14, etc., who partly sojourns in the world and partly reigns with the Lord, desires to be heard by the King of all ages. For no one. No one with the corruption of the present life can enter the heavenly court, but before his death each ought by chastening of body and compunction of heart to knock at the entrance of the kingdom, that afterwards rejoicing he may enter the heavenly palace. If anyone asks how the most just King inflicts torments on the innocent, let him know that this is not from a will of malice, but proceeds from the nod of the supreme counsel. For wisdom overcomes malice, Wisdom 7, reaches from end to end mightily: and orders all things sweetly, ibid., 8. Whatsoever he pleased he has done in heaven and in all the depths, Psalm 113. By whose just judgment it happens that the faithful are delivered into the hand of persecutors either for purgation, or for correction, or for the increase of merits: so Job is delivered to Satan; Paul is buffeted by an angel of Satan. Again. Mordecai and Esther pray for each other, that is masters and disciples, as Paul prays for his disciples, and begs to be prayed for, as in the Acts of the Apostles prayer was made without ceasing by the Church for Peter.
5.2: 5.2 The golden scepter. The power of rule or the cross of the passion, through which he acquired power, of which it is said: All power is given to me in heaven and on earth, Matthew 28. And elsewhere: Wherefore God has exalted him, and has given him a name which is above all names, Philippians 2.
5.8: 5.8 If I have found in the sight. Delay in asking is not reckoned to sloth, but to patience. For not in the present but in the future will reward be repaid to the good and the wicked: for tomorrow is put for the future, hence: Be not solicitous for tomorrow; and Jacob in Genesis says: My justice shall answer for me tomorrow, Matthew 6. And of the lamb it is said: There shall not remain any of it until morning, Genesis 30. When judgment comes, it will be revealed in what garment each has entered the banquet.
6.1: 6.1 That night the king passed sleepless, etc. Remaining unchangeable in himself, he contemplates the course of times and the acts of all, and no thought is hidden from him to whom all things are present; hence the Apostle: There is not in him, it is and it was, but in him it is always, 2 Corinthians 1.
6.2: 6.2 It was come to. The deeds of Mordecai are recalled before the king; because the good works of holy teachers will never be given to oblivion, but the just shall be in eternal memory.
6.10: 6.10 Make haste. The masters of the Church, illustrated by the cultivation of all virtues and the beauty of wisdom, are honored with the diadem of royal dignity, as members of the supreme King. They ride on the royal horse, that is, upon the people of the faithful in whose hearts the King of angels dwells; hence the prophet Habakkuk: Mounting upon your horses, and your riding is salvation. To these Haman, special enemy of the people of God, although unwilling, renders service when the persecutors of the Church are forced to give testimony to the Church itself, unable to hide what is manifest. He took therefore. This is the change of the right hand of the Most High, who if he seemed more glorious, appears below the others, viler and lower, according to that: He has put down the mighty from their seat, and exalted the humble. Likewise Isaiah says: Lebanon shall be turned into Carmel, and Carmel shall be reputed as a forest. So the pride of the Synagogue was crushed, the humility of the Church exalted. So the persecutors of the faith were reduced to nothing: the confessors of Christ exalted in the whole world. The head turned into the tail, and the tail into the head: for everyone that exalts himself shall be humbled, Luke 24.
7.1: 7.1 On the second day, etc. But when Esther opened her petition, the condemned went out to punishment. For in the Gospel a dinner and a supper are mentioned. The dinner designates the present time of the Church, but the supper the eternal and last banquet. Hence, the wicked being separated, the good rejoice forever. Haman, because he had not a garment worthy of the banquet, deserved to be cast out.
7.7: 7.7 He went into the garden. The king hastening into the garden, that is, inviting the elect with himself to the delights of paradise, Haman strives to plead with the queen for his safety, but had not a favorable time. For the remedies of salvation are sought too late, when the dangers of death are at hand; hence Solomon: Then shall they call upon me, and I will not hear: they shall rise in the morning, and shall not find me, Proverbs 1.
7.8: 7.8 And immediately. The pleading of Haman is called oppression, because on the day of judgment the prayer of the wicked is provocation: hence: When he is judged, let him go out condemned, Psalm 108, etc. Then the oppression with which they oppressed the humble will be cast in their teeth.
7.9: 7.9 Harbona. He signifies the teachers of the law, who foretold the crimes and deceits of the Jews, hence Moses: I know that after my death you will act wickedly, and turn aside from the way which I have shown you, Deuteronomy 31. And in the Gospel: There is one that accuses you, Moses, in whom you trust, John 5. In the house of Haman. It signifies the wicked tumultuating against Christ, Haman and his Church persecuting. Christ, however, was promised to them in the law; the law therefore, which was given for the keeping of life, was turned to death for them, through which they attempted to destroy Christ and kill his confessors: and those who by the law wished to oppress the innocent, the law itself accusing, received the sentence of just judgment. Those who have sinned in the law shall be avenged by the law.
8.1: 8.1 On that day. Esther holds the house of Haman, enemy of the Jews, when the Church possesses the world, which the devil, enemy of Christians, had possessed; hence: When the strong man armed keeps his court, Luke 11, etc. Mordecai enters before the face of the king, when daily the souls of the saints enter from the dwelling of the present life to the contemplation of the divine majesty. The house of Haman. The dignity and honor which the Jews had by knowledge of the law and of the prophets and the worship of religion; hence in Proverbs: The substance of the sinner is kept for the just, Proverbs 13. And in the Gospel: The kingdom shall be taken from you, and given to a nation yielding the fruits thereof, Matthew 21.
8.2: 8.2 And the king took. The masters, praising and preaching with earnestness, receive from the Lord grace for grace in the sight of the Maker of all; hence: He fed the hearts of the faithful. He delivered to Mordecai. To the preachers of the Gentiles, that they might cling to him and minister to the Gentiles.
8.3: 8.3 She fell at his feet, etc. Because holy Church, for the rescue of her children, daily entreats God almighty through faith and the mysteries of the incarnation, that the boldness of enemies be repressed and the innocence of the faithful be delivered.
8.5: 8.5 I beseech that. Because the evangelical doctrine, which is preached in the name of Christ in the whole world, is declared confirmed by the seal of the Holy Spirit, by whose gift the preachers themselves, filled, remained unconquerable and glorious triumphers over their enemies.
8.9: 8.9 And the scribes being called, etc. Because the doctrine of the Gospel was so composed by the writers of the New Testament, the Lord mediating, that the faith of the holy Trinity is most fully contained in it, and the perfection of the whole decalogue is shown in the two precepts of charity. Who a hundred and twenty. In whom the whole world is signified. For ten multiplied by twelve makes a hundred and twenty, to which seven joined concludes the fullness of the whole sum: so the keeping of the decalogue, spread through the whole world by apostolic tradition, the grace of the sevenfold Spirit is poured into the hearts of the faithful or is consummated.
8.11: 8.11 To kill, etc. Lest the seedbeds of an evil seed spring up again. Likewise the seven nations that dwelt in the land of promise the Lord commanded to be killed, and afterwards the Amalekites to be wholly destroyed, that he might take away from them every occasion of scandal; hence David says: In the morning I killed, Psalm 100, etc.
8.14: 8.14 In Susa, etc. To subdue the pride of the world. For Susa is interpreted riding or overturning; hence the Savior says: Be of good cheer, I have overcome the world, John 16.
9.4: 9.4 And knew that he could do much. Because the praiseworthy action of teachers and the power of virtues give honor and reverence to the multitude of the faithful. Hence in the Acts of the Apostles: Many wonders and signs were done, Acts 5, hence it is read elsewhere: And fear came upon every soul, ibid. 2. Likewise: None durst join himself to them, but the people magnified them, ibid. 5.
9.5: 9.5 So the Jews struck. The divine sentence of the Holy Spirit judges not only other workers of iniquity, who persevere in sins and do not care to receive remission of sins, to be condemned, but also carnal Jews, transgressors of the decalogue, to feel in the cities of hell the guilt of the cross of Christ which they contracted through perfidy.
9.6: 9.6 Whose names are these. The interpretations of these names we do not seek out with much labor, nor compel them to serve allegory. For a type is in part, not in the whole. For if it is a type in the whole, it is not history. The historian must set forth the true series of the deed done, neither stopping short nor going beyond: the allegorical interpreter must choose the excellent parts that agree in the spiritual sense.
9.16: 9.16 So far. All who receive the law carnally with the five bodily senses, and, while it is specially full and perfect through the sevenfold grace of the Holy Spirit, refuse to understand it spiritually, are as it were conquered and laid low in two days.
9.17: 9.17 But the day. It is to be noted that some of the Jews kill on the thirteenth day, and cease on the fourteenth, and keep the solemnity; others for two days, that is on the thirteenth and fourteenth day of the same month they kill, on the fifteenth they rest solemnly: because some of the saints, after completing the labors in which they serve God by believing well and living well, now before the time of judgment have in their souls the sabbath of eternal rest: others, persevering in the flesh until the last day of the resurrection, all enemies being overcome, suddenly changed, receive rest of souls and bodies; hence the Apostle: The dead who are in Christ shall rise first. Then we who are alive, who are left, shall be taken up together with them to meet Christ in the air, 1 Thessalonians 4, etc. For the fourteenth, which contains twice seven, signifies the perfect rest of souls, but the fifteenth, embracing seven and eight, signifies the rest of souls and bodies.
9.24: 9.24 And cast Pur, etc. The lot cast into the urn signifies the disposition of anything in the mind of man, whose event is ruled not by human but by divine judgment, hence Solomon: Lots are cast into the lap, but they are ordered by the Lord, Proverbs 16.
9.28: 9.28 These are the days. Because the rest of souls and the resurrection of bodies is deservedly firmly kept and celebrated by the faithful: or, because the holiday of the rest of souls and the resurrection of bodies is deservedly kept and celebrated by the faithful.
10.1: 10.1 And King Ahasuerus all the. Christ, who, cut out of the mountain without hands, grew into a great mountain and filled the whole world: for historically he did not make the whole earth tributary, because he did not have it. In the ancient copies of the ordinary Glossa, no exposition lies beside the sacred text from here to the end of the book. Therefore we pass over chapters 11-16.
